Every tile leans the same three or four colours — espresso ground, antique gold, a single ember accent for warmth, never more than one bright note per frame. That restraint is what makes twelve unrelated photographs read as one shelf.

How this becomes the poster

  • Ground: the near-black espresso from every backdrop here, not a flat black — it already reads warm.
  • Accent: one antique gold, used sparingly — a rule, a label, a cap — the way it appears once per photo, not everywhere.
  • Texture over icon: petals, smoke, wax — real material stands in for decorative ornament.
  • One bright bottle per frame: the product should be the only lit thing in the shot, same as the flat-lays here.
